title: Streaming resume + soft-discard reconciliation for interrupted generations
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe two classes of customer-visible failures when clients disconnect mid-generation: 1) orphaned partial outputs that accumulate in ephemeral caches and increase memory/GC pressure, and 2) inability for well-behaved clients to resume generation because resume proofs (resume tokens) don't survive soft aborts or are rendered incompatible after aggressive prefix compaction.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic, low-latency resume handshake that allows clients to pick up interrupted generations without opening a fresh inference run where possible.
- Introduce a 'soft-discard' mechanism that allows the runtime to reclaim resources early but still retain minimal resume metadata for a bounded window.
- Ensure function/tool-call atomicity and structured-output integrity when resuming: tool call side effects must not be replayed or leaked.
- Avoid regressions to latency/SLOs from extra bookkeeping; keep per-request steady-state overhead minimal.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Generation slices: split live generations into small sequence-aligned slices with monotonic slice IDs. Each slice is checkpointed as a compact prefix-signature rather than full token sequence.
2) Resume proof: when a client disconnects, the server issues a short-lived resume token that includes (slice_id, prefix_sig, epoch, lease_expiry) signed by the control-plane signing key. Clients present this token to attempt resume; the runtime validates the prefix signature to ensure the cached KV state matches.
3) Soft-discard window: soft-discard allows the runtime to evict bulky ephemeral payloads (partial logits, big KV fragments) while keeping prefix_sig + minimal KV digests for a configurable TTL (default 5 minutes). After TTL the resume token is rejected and generation is considered orphaned and eligible for hard GC.
4) Tool/function-call isolation: slices that contain function calls mark an execution boundary. Resume is permitted only at slice boundaries where no in-flight side-effect exists; for any slice with a tool call the runtime records a idempotency marker and high-water state. If resume is attempted past a function-call slice, resume fails and client must re-run with information returned by the last committed tool-call.
5) Compatibility shim: to support older SDKs and other backends we implement a compatibility layer that accepts legacy resume tokens and maps them to the new resume proof format where possible, otherwise returns structured error guidance with recommended client migration steps.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Keeping full prefixes for long TTL would make resume trivial but increases memory and disk pressure. We trade memory for cryptographic prefix signatures (SHA256 of KV deltas) to keep state small.
- Allowing resume across function calls simplifies UX but risks double-execution. We restrict resume across function-call boundaries and require idempotency markers for tool call handlers.
- Increasing TTL improves UX for unreliable mobile clients but raises resource usage; default 5 minutes balances most observed disconnect patterns vs cluster pressure.

Implementation notes / APIs: 
- New non-streaming API: POST /v1/resume-validate -> validate token, returns resumeable: true/false and earliest_slice.
- Streaming handshake extension: on initial open the client may send resume_token; if accepted the server returns resume_ack with last_seq and reinflated KV pointers.
- Runtime metadata: per-generation state becomes: generation_id (string), current_slice (int), prefix_sig (hex), resume_expiry (RFC3339), function_boundary_flags (comma-separated slice IDs), lease_owner (string). All persisted compactly to the ephemeral store (rocksdb shard) keyed by generation_id.

Safety and correctness: 
- Tokens signed by control-plane key; token replay across tenants is impossible due to tenant_id binding.
- Resume validation checks model checkpoint compatibility (model-id + weights-checksum) to avoid mismatches after rollouts; if mismatch, server returns structured JSON guidance with next steps.

Observability / metrics:
- streaming.resume.attempts, streaming.resume.success, streaming.resume.failures.reason (token-expired|model-mismatch|tool-boundary), streaming.soft_discard.evictions, streaming.partial_gc.rate, streaming.avg-time-to-reclaim.
- Add per-tenant metric that correlates resume success with SLO impact (latency reduction, token savings).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for token serialization and prefix-signature validation.
- Integration tests simulating flaky clients: network drop at various sequence offsets, resume attempts inside and outside function-call slices.
- Chaos test: kill worker during streaming flush and assert resume token validity; ensure no tool-call double-exec by mocking tool connectors.
- Load test: measure memory and latency impact at 10k concurrent interrupted streams with 5-minute TTL and a 30s TTL baseline.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary runtime flag gated rollout to subset of customers (internal + 3 pilot tenants).
2) Telemetry watch: track resume success rate and partial GC growth for two weeks.
3) Gradual ramp with runtime-2.4 release if metrics stable.
4) SDK updates: publish client-side helpers that automatically request and present resume tokens; compatibility shim accepts legacy tokens for 6 weeks.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence) and open design review scheduled.
